findings.detail: The inference.md patch (head lines 684-691) documents that coordinator-mode registration will publish a cached manifest aggregate (`GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256`, `VerifiedWeightHashStore`) without reading the weights. It will skip the read while each file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are unchanged. This is a documentation-only change, so it is not a code regression. It does create an attack surface that T-012 (operator replaces model weights) and T-027 (weight substitution) do not describe. An operator with write access could modify weight bytes in place and then restore mtime. ctime cannot be set from userland, but a replace-and-rename or a write that evades the identity check could still be a gap. The load "verifies again before serving", which narrows the window, but the registered hash is not itself freshly verified. The threat model should record this trust assumption and its limits.
findings.title: Docs now say the GLM5-Next weight hash is the manifest aggregate, with later starts skipping a weight read (T-012 / T-027 / T-034 assumptions)
